evidence: Quint. 1.6.10: faceret tempore praeteritō pactus sum
Quint. 1.4.28: quaedam etiam mūtantur ut ferō in praeteritō
terms.comment: praeteritum alone also serves, in praeteritō, in the past (Quintilian). The grammarians divided it into praeteritum imperfectum, perfectum and plūsquamperfectum (see those tenses).

phrases.latin: quia prīma positiō pacīscor, cum habēret nātūram patiendī, faceret tempore praeteritō pactus sum
phrases.english: because the first form pacīscor, having the nature of a passive, would make pactus sum in the past tense

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 248.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
